nodes.title: Pavel Holman
nodes.summary: AI engineer and co-founder; leads small teams that ship products; three-time ICPC finalist. Open to remote work and thesis-linked collaboration.
nodes.body:
Pavel Holman is a Prague software engineer finishing a master's degree in Artificial Intelligence at CTU FEE (expected June 2027) after a bachelor's in AI at CTU FIT. He co-founded DeelsCorp (2024) and poqet (2026) and is the principal engineer of both: he led the four-person Deels team across mobile apps, a Kotlin backend, APIs and infrastructure, and now leads the three-person SLIM team while owning its agent-assisted development process. Part-time at Merica since 2020 on C# business software. ICPC finalist at CERC 2024, CERC 2025 and EUC 2026.

Strongest skills: TypeScript with Effect, Kotlin, and agentic engineering. He prefers practical impact over theory, typed and explicit systems, and claims backed by evidence, which is why this portfolio answers from a knowledge graph with citations. Interests: programming languages (Kotlin, Swift, Rust), functional programming, algorithms, and neuro-symbolic AI and automated experimentation as areas he is curious about.

fields.headline: AI engineer and co-founder
fields.lede: AI master's student at CTU and co-founder of two shipped products. I lead small teams end to end, from Kotlin backends and multiplatform apps at Deels to a SvelteKit and Effect lab platform at poqet, with agentic development tooling that keeps both honest. ICPC finalist, three times.
fields.availability: Open to remote work and to a thesis-linked research or engineering collaboration alongside the master's degree.

languages.English: professional working proficiency (Cambridge English First, B2)

nodes.title: Agentic engineering
nodes.summary: Claude Code harnesses, guardrails and evals that let a small team ship fast; one of Pavel's three strongest skills.
nodes.body: Building the tooling that makes coding agents reliable: a Claude Code development harness with TypeScript automation, architectural rules and guardrails, and evaluations, so a three-person team can develop SLIM at poqet with agents doing much of the work. The same approach built this portfolio from written specs and ADRs with lint rules and evals as guardrails.

nodes.title: Deels
nodes.summary: Marketplace for gastro discounts, loyalty programmes and surplus food, used by 80 partners in Prague.
nodes.body: Deels is a marketplace connecting gastro businesses and customers in Prague. Businesses reach customers through discounts and loyalty programmes, including discounted food that would otherwise go to waste; customers discover places at lower prices. Used by about 80 gastro partners in Prague. Built by a four-person team led by Pavel Holman: Kotlin backend with PostgreSQL and a GraphQL API, mobile apps in Kotlin Multiplatform, Compose Multiplatform and SwiftUI, services in Docker, hosted on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Backed by a CZK 1 million grant from CzechInvest's Technology Incubation programme. Shipped; now in maintenance.

nodes.title: Employee rostering with constraint programming
nodes.summary: Shift rostering solver built in C# with Google OR-Tools and OptalCP in a two-person team; Pavel led the modelling.
nodes.body: An employee rostering project at Merica: assigning staff to shifts under availability, legal and business constraints, modelled as a constraint program and solved with Google OR-Tools and OptalCP, delivered as part of C# business software. Built in a two-person team, with Pavel leading the constraint modelling and solver work.

nodes.title: Forecasting energy costs in day-ahead and intraday markets
nodes.summary: Bachelor's thesis: AutoML pipeline forecasting electricity prices from market, weather and grid data.
nodes.body: Bachelor's thesis at CTU FIT (2025). Built an automated, modular electricity-price forecasting pipeline with AutoGluon and pandas, integrating OTE market data, Open-Meteo weather observations and forecasts, and ENTSO-E power-grid data, with cleaning, transformation and merging of multi-source time series. Forecasting tasks: seven-day hourly forecasts for the day-ahead market and one-day forecasts at 15-minute resolution for the intraday market. Compared statistical, machine-learning and deep-learning models against simple baselines using chronological splits and multi-window evaluation; traditional machine-learning models (gradient-boosted trees and random forests) beat the deep-learning models on this data, a result Pavel values for the simplicity and explainability of the winning models. Noted limitations: weather-forecast availability, a short historical window, and extreme price spikes.

nodes.body: FERP is Merica's ERP system for Czech companies. Pavel developed features in it and built the data loaders around it that import and synchronise data from customers' systems and files, and took part in moving the stack from .NET Framework to .NET Core.

nodes.title: GraphRAG Portfolio
nodes.summary: This site. A 3D resume that answers questions from a knowledge graph and highlights its evidence.
nodes.body: Pavel's personal interactive 3D portfolio: a visitor asks a question or pastes a job description, retrieval selects a subgraph of his professional history, one streamed LLM call answers with inline citations, and the 3D scene highlights the cited nodes as they arrive. Hand-authored Markdown nodes with typed frontmatter are validated and embedded at build time into a committed artifact; the runtime is a stateless Cloudflare Worker. Lint rules forbid `throw` and `Date` in favour of Effect and Temporal.

nodes.title: SLIM
nodes.summary: Lab operations platform for academic laboratories; samples, inventory, equipment, notebooks, multi-lab access control.
nodes.body: SLIM is poqet's lab operations platform for academic laboratories in botany, biology and chemistry: sample tracking, inventory and warehouses, projects and tasks, equipment and reservations, lab notebooks and protocols, several laboratories within one institute, and a role- and permission-based access system. Used by research groups at three Prague institutions. Full-stack web application in SvelteKit, Effect and SurrealDB, built by a three-person team led by Pavel Holman.

nodes.body: Co-founder and principal engineer of DeelsCorp since May 2024. Led engineering end to end for a four-person team: mobile applications, backend services, APIs and infrastructure. Backend in Kotlin with PostgreSQL; apps with Kotlin Multiplatform, Compose Multiplatform and SwiftUI; GraphQL API; Docker for services. Backend in Kotlin with PostgreSQL, exposed through PostGraphile behind a GraphQL Hive and Mesh gateway, hosted on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure.
